newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Bass set for 10 pct profits rise.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Bass set for 10 pct profits rise.

text.p: Brewer-to-hotel group Bass Plc is expected to report a 10-percent rise in its half-year profits on Wednesday, driven by its managed pub estate and its 2,200 strong Holiday Inn empire.
Analysts' forecasts for pretax profits range from 305 to 325 million stg, up from 289 million last time. A dividend payout of 8.4p per share is expected, up from 7.7p.
"The main thing driving their profits will be growth in sales at their pubs and the strength of their beer brands and distribution," said Lehman Brothers analyst Fraser Ramzan.
Lehman forecast pretax profits of 319 million stg, but warn the results will be overshadowed by an imminent decision from government about whether Bass can acquire Carlsberg-Tetley.

The company is forecast to turn in about 85 million stg from its brewing business helped by a contribution of some 10 million stg from C-T. Under the terms of a deal agreed with Allied Domecq Plc last August Bass retains half of the profits from C-T until the deal is concluded.
The acquisition is currently being reviewed by the new incoming Labour government which is widely expected to impose more stringent conditions or block the deal altogether.

On average analysts expect Bass's pub retailing business, which includes Harvester pub-restaurants, to contribute about 145 million stg to group profits, up from 135 million last time, and Holiday Inns about 81 million as against 76 million last time.

The leisure division, which includes Gala bingo clubs and Coral betting shops, is forecast to chip in 35 million and soft drinks about eight million. An interest charge of about 40 million is expected.
In February Bass chairman Sir Ian Posser warned that the business was running slightly behind its forecasts, sending its shares tumbling.
"In the first 16 weeks of the year, the business has continued to make progress, although slightly behind our expectations," Prosser told shareholders.

Bass shares were 13p lower at 816p on Friday, against a high for the year of 879 and a low of 505p. Uncertainty over the outcome of Bass's bid for Carlsberg Tetley has continued to depress the share price.
"You have to remember that the chairman has a tendency to understate the positive and overstate the negative," said Nikko analyst Dermot Carr.
